newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares plunge at close on foreign selling. [CORRECTED 04:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Manila shares plunge at close on foreign selling. [CORRECTED 04:51 GMT]

text.p: * Dow's advance fails to energise local equities market

The Manila share index dived by 60.27 points, or 2.23 percent, to 2,648.17 points at close on Wednesday on foreign selling which was worsened by unflattering first quarter earnings of major companies, traders said.

"It's continued foreign selling pressure. It's really a bear market and people now are looking at the bad side of earnings instead of the good side," Joey Roxas (corrects from "Salceda"), president at Eagle equities Inc said.
Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities said that even the Dow's phenomenal rise overnight failed to spark interest in the market soured by disappointing first quarter company profits.
The Dow ended higher on Tuesday by 179.01 points at 6,962.03.
Foreign selling was prominent as B shares of San Miguel Corp, Manila Electric Co and Ayala Land Inc were being sold during the session.
Turnover, however, was lower at 2.37 billion pesos compared with 3.67 billion the previous session.
Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities said the market may persist in its downslide simply due to a lack of positive news to provide a brake.
The stock market will be closed on Thursday to mark the Labor Day and traders said this may have influenced investors to take short positions.
